newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, New Zealand central bank sign repo pact.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, New Zealand central bank sign repo pact.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) said they signed a bilateral repurchase agreement on Wednesday.
The deal was signed by visiting RBNZ governor Don Brash and Joseph Yam, chief executive of HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank, they said in a statement.

The HKMA, Hong Kong's de facto central bank, has already signed bilateral repo agreements with the central banks of nine other Asian nations -- Australia, China, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea and Thailand.
The repo pacts are part of an effort among Asian countries to cooperate more in financial matters to avoid the type of crisis Mexico suffered in late 1994 when its currency came under attack.
The bilateral agreement allows the parties to enhance the liquidity of its foreign reserves portfolio with minimal additional risks, they said.
Highly liquid U.S. dollar government securities are the instruments used in all the repurchase agreements signed between the HKMA and regional central banks.
